newsitem.title: UK: Outlook for April UK RPI - ONS.
newsitem.headline: Outlook for April UK RPI - ONS.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics said the following factors, already in the public domain, would probably affect the April retail price index.

Seasonal food prices would normally be expected to be flat or lower in April, but because of their unusual behaviour recently, experts are hesitating to make predictions, but there is a question mark over whether dry weather conditions will have an impact.
Overall food prices fell by an annual 1.6 percent in March, the sharpest fall since April 1960 when there was a fall of 1.8 percent.
Council tax rises of around 6.6 percent and water and sewerage charge increases of around 4.0 percent are set to kick in in April.

Changes announced at the November budget also come into effect, including an increase in insurance premium tax to 4.0 percent from 2.5 percent, higher prices for colour television licences, now 91.50 stg, up from 89.50 stg and prescription charge rises of 15 pence, taking the price to 5.65 stg.
But possibly exerting downward pressure, a number of electricity companies have announced price cuts for April, the ONS said.
